annotation.title_clean: Technology at Work v2.0: The Future Is Not What It Used to Be
annotation.title_en: Technology at Work v2.0: The Future Is Not What It Used to Be
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Frey, C.B.; Osborne, M.A.; Holmes, C.; Rahbari, E.; Curmi, E.; Garlick, R.; et al. (Citi GPS / Oxford Martin School)
annotation.summary_en: Citi GPS report co-produced with the Oxford Martin School examining automation's impact on jobs worldwide and across cities, sector effects, productivity and inflation, and policy responses including education, job creation and a chapter on robot laws (privacy, ethics, liability). Main focus is labour-market disruption rather than governance of physical robots.
key_provisions_or_claims: 47% of US jobs at risk from automation; risk is higher in many developing countries (e.g., 77% China, 69% India)
Perception and manipulation, creative intelligence and social intelligence are bottlenecks to automation
Payback periods for industrial robot systems are falling, threatening offshoring trends
Education investment and technological dynamism are key policy responses
Robot laws on privacy, ethics and liability may slow the pace of automation
